questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing does not protect you.
No, clothing is just a personal choice.
Yes, but only if clothes are very loose and flap in the wind.
Yes, if you wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if you wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs.
questions.explanation: Good clothing can reduce injury in a crash. Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, are made of sturdy material, and fit snugly so they do not flap.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after drinking one drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.
Alcohol may still affect your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol may still affect your body.
questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour. However, the time varies for each person. The safest choice is not to ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: You should fully check your motorcycle:
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent checks than cars. Check your motorcycle completely before every ride.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per drink before riding your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your skills will not be affected.
You will be fine if you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still remain.
questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour. But alcohol can build up in your system even if you drink slowly. This buildup can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: What is the most important safety equipment a rider must wear?
questions.correctAnswerText: A helmet
questions.explanation: A helmet is the most important safety equipment you can wear. One in five motorcycle crashes causes head and neck injuries. A helmet greatly improves your chances of survival.

questions.question: The best source of information about your motorcycle is:
questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Read your owner's manual first. It tells you how your specific motorcycle works, what it needs, and how to maintain it.

questions.question: A motorcycle needs:

options.text: Less frequent checks than a car.
More frequent checks than a car.
Checks only by a mechanic before each ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: More frequent checks than a car.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for a motorcycle rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or high-top shoes give the best protection. They support your ankles. Laced boots are best, but high-top boots or heavy shoes work too. Tuck in long laces before riding.

questions.question: The best source of information about your motorcycle is:
questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are borrowing someone else's motorcycle.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket or pants, look for:
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather material.
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs. Leather provides the best protection.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: During the day and at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the day and at night.
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing helps other drivers see you in any conditions. Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day, so wear bright clothing at all times.

questions.question: What is a benefit of wearing gloves?

options.text: They make it harder to control the motorcycle and should be avoided.
They help other drivers notice you.
They give you a better grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves give you a better grip on the handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: What type of pants protect motorcycle riders best?

options.text: Loose pants that flap in the wind.
Short pants that expose your legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy material pants.
questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or sturdy material that cover your entire legs. The pants should fit snugly so they don't flap in the wind, but not so tight that they limit your movement.

questions.question: How should you handle a driver tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to get away from them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up only makes them tailgate at higher speeds, creating more danger.

questions.question: How should you use the front brake?

options.text: It is too dangerous for new riders to use.
Use it only sometimes to help the rear brake.
Use it together with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use it together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When should you check your mirrors?

options.text: As part of your regular scanning routine.
They don't help since you can't do anything about what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: As part of your regular scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal scanning routine. Always check your mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: What should you consider when choosing a lane position?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead on the road.
Which position makes your trip shorter.
Which position lets you pass more vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose your lane position to make sure other drivers can see you. You should also keep enough space between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: What helmet provides the most protection?

options.text: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
A helmet that has been in a previous crash.
A helmet that protects your hearing.

questions.correctAnswerText: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state safety standards. The helmet should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator slow down?
questions.correctAnswerText: By downshifting.
questions.explanation: You can slow down by downshifting. Be aware that downshifting does not activate your brake lights.

questions.question: How can you help other drivers see you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright clothing, keep your headlight on at all times, and always use your turn signals.

questions.question: When you cannot avoid an object or uneven surface, what should you do?

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle, approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Slow down as much as you can. Keep your motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off your seat so your knees can absorb the force. Just before impact, roll on the throttle slightly to lift the front end.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to handle differently while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over and check the chain.
Pull over and check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A change in handling usually means a tire has failed. If you notice a change in how your motorcycle handles, pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet that is fastened securely is the most effective action you can take to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: What reduces the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most effective way to reduce the risk of head or neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: What should passengers do on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when the operator leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean with them. Sit as close to the operator as possible without crowding them. Hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Which of these does not protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: A baseball cap that fits snugly

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap that fits snugly
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: Why are signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They matter less since motorcycles are smaller than other vehicles.
They alert other drivers to what you plan to do.
You only need to use them if vehicles are nearby.
They are more complicated than car signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: They alert other drivers to what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are more vulnerable, so it is very important to use turn signals to alert others to your plans. Always use them when changing lanes or turning, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
It keeps you in one area of the lane and limits your movement.
It means you can rely on others to spot dangers.
It requires you to go faster to keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle helps you have time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: How can a rider prevent injury on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, decrease your speed. Sudden moves can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid a slippery road.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle?

options.text: Ride it like your own bike since all bikes are similar.
Check the controls and gear shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works.
Assume you know where all controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and gear shift pattern.
questions.explanation: All motorcycles are different, so check the controls and learn the gear pattern before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle. Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes several times before you ride.
